topic: Someone receives a package intended for the previous tenant
text: The rain drums against the window, steady as a heartbeat. I slide the package across the scarred wood of my desk, eyeing it like it's a coiled snake. This ain't meant for me, but it landed on my doorstep all the same, wrapped up neat with a bow on top. Names and addresses, they're a funny thing—move too slow, and the world keeps on spinning, leaving you behind. The handwriting's careful, almost fancy, but that don’t mean nothing. I know folks who could charm the birds from the trees, then stick you for every dime you got. I pull a pen from my pocket, weighing it in my hand. Maybe it’s just a mix-up, mail gone astray. But in this city, you don't open anything you don’t have to. Not if you want to live to see tomorrow.
